The failure occurs in the test `testOverrideMeanWithMathClass` of the `SummaryStatisticsTest` class from Apache Commons Math library. The test sets an implementation for mean calculation using the `Mean` class and then calculates the mean of a set of scores using the `SummaryStatistics` class. The test then asserts that the calculated mean matches the mean calculated by the `Mean` class.

The current bug report states that invoking `setVarianceImpl(new Variance(true/false)` makes `getStandardDeviation` produce `NaN`. This issue appears to be related to setting the variance implementation in the `SummaryStatistics` class.

By looking at the code snippet of the `SummaryStatistics` class method `setVarianceImpl`, it can be seen that it sets the provided variance implementation without applying any additional calculation or validation. This method simply assigns the variance implementation without further checks.

On the other hand, the `getStandardDeviation` method in the `SynchronizedDescriptiveStatistics` class (a superclass of `SummaryStatistics`) is overridden to return the standard deviation without any extra logic or handling.

Therefore, the issue seems to be that setting the variance implementation directly without appropriate validation or calculation leads to incorrect results when calculating the standard deviation with `getStandardDeviation`.

To fix this issue, validation or calculation checks should be added in the `setVarianceImpl` method to ensure that setting the variance implementation does not cause incorrect results in the standard deviation calculation.

Suggestions for fixing:
```
org.apache.commons.math3.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(org.apache.commons.math3.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
